There is so much misunderstanding about what AI actually does in our classrooms. It’s not chatbots, we call them “cheatbots.” It’s also not an open-loop free access setup where students type in “teach me long division” or “what’s the answer?” It’s education software, learning apps based on common core curriculum that uses AI to evaluate students so they can be placed in the right level of curriculum they need. This is huge! It’s what human tutors do so well-but in a school setting with 15-30 students per class a teacher can’t be like a human tutor-until now. Another key point, the AI assesses what pace-how fast or slow to progress each student, so they aren’t bored but also aren’t lost. The AI measures within the learning app when a student has mastered the material- then and only then will it move on. And of course this doesn’t negate the role of humans, none of this is possible without a caring, supportive human providing that motivation and accountability to every student. 👨‍🎓📝📚💻

🚩🚩🚩The classrooms are designed to prioritize the teacher-in-front-of-the-classroom model. Think one teacher’s desk at the front of the room at the white board, and a room full of desks all lined up neatly in rows. 

What it actually should be? Classrooms that prioritize group discussions, collaboration, and free thinking. Maybe desks are in a big circle in the room, or clumped into groups. Maybe there are no desks! 🤷🏼‍♀️

🚩🚩🚩No focus on teaching kids socialization. Traditional schools throw kids into the deep end and expect them to swim. (Many sink 🥺🦈)

Kids need to be taught how to be interesting, and how to be interested in others. How to give and receive feedback. How to debate and discuss ideas. How to create a culture of belonging and foster teamwork. Just because the school has a lot of students doesn’t mean these skills will develop.

🚩🚩🚩Grade inflation and social promotion. Teachers not allowed to fail students or hold them back. This is a HUGE issue right now and it’s bankrupting our kids of their education. Kids are being pushed from grade to grade despite not truly being ready. 

The scary part? Many parents have no idea. This past year, we had an influx of new students across our campuses and found that even the A and B students were actually *several* grade levels behind. 🫣 They had no idea and neither did their parents. 

🚩🚩🚩Teachers saddled with way too many job requirements and low pay. These teachers cannot possibly do their jobs well when scope creep continues like this.

#1-Homework. We don’t give it and we don’t need it for kids to excel at academics. AND we only use 2 hours a day for academics, the rest of the day are life-skills workshops.

#2- Tradition & Keeping Things The Same- 
We are like the iPhone, we iterate every year. We change our AI learning app software to apps that are better, change our school schedule to accommodate families better, move the entire school to a better facility in the middle of the year-ALWAYS improving!

#3 Every students’ progress is on the wall and public.

#4- Fail often and fail fast. Tradition school punishes kids for failure, get a C on a report card, transcript and college future is ruined. This discourages experimentation and trying new things, which forces kids into a fixed mentality.  We foster a growth mindset in all areas! 

#5- Having incredibly high standards. 
We have high standards but offer high support. Kids actually love being challenged, whether it’s in academics, sports, the arts, whatever.
